theorem map_units_restrict_basicOpen {R : CommRingCat.{u}} (M : (Spec R).Modules) (f : R) :
    ∀ x : Submonoid.powers f, IsUnit (algebraMap R (Module.End R
      ((modulesSpecToSheaf.obj M).presheaf.obj
        (.op (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen f)))) (x : R)) := by
  rintro ⟨x, n, rfl⟩
  rw [map_pow]
  exact (Scheme.Modules.isUnit_algebraMap_end_of_le_basicOpen (M := M) f le_rfl).pow n

/-- **Finite basic-open cover refining a quasi-coherent presentation cover.** Given a
sheaf of modules `M` on `Spec R` together with quasi-coherent data `q` (a — possibly
infinite — open cover `q.X : q.I → (Spec R).Opens` of `⊤` with a presentation of
`M.over (q.X i)` on each member), there is a *finite* family of elements `t : Finset R`
whose basic opens cover `Spec R` (`Ideal.span t = ⊤`), with each basic open `D(r)`
(`r ∈ t`) contained in some member `q.X i` of the presentation cover.

theorem exists_finite_basicOpen_cover_le_quasicoherentData {R : CommRingCat.{u}}
    (M : (Spec R).Modules) (q : M.QuasicoherentData) :
    ∃ t : Finset R, Ideal.span (t : Set R) = ⊤ ∧
      ∀ r ∈ t, ∃ i, (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : (Spec R).Opens) ≤ q.X i := by
  classical
  set G : Set R := {r | ∃ i, (PrimeSpectrum.basicOpen r : (Spec R).Opens) ≤ q.X i} with hG
  have hspanG : Ideal.span G = ⊤ := by
    rw [← PrimeSpectrum.iSup_basicOpen_eq_top_iff']
    rw [eq_top_iff]
    intro x _
    simp only [TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_iSup]
    obtain ⟨U, f, hf, hxU⟩ := q.coversTop ⊤ x (by trivial)
    rw [Sieve.mem_ofObjects_iff] at hf
    obtain ⟨i, ⟨hUi⟩⟩ := hf
    have hxXi : x ∈ q.X i := (leOfHom hUi) hxU
    obtain ⟨V, ⟨r, rfl⟩, hxV, hVle⟩ :=
      (TopologicalSpace.Opens.isBasis_iff_nbhd.mp PrimeSpectrum.isBasis_basic_opens) hxXi

theorem isQuasicoherent_pullback_of_isOpenImmersion {Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : Y ⟶ X)
    [IsOpenImmersion g] (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj M).IsQuasicoherent := by
  obtain ⟨q⟩ : Nonempty M.QuasicoherentData :=
    SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.nonempty_quasicoherentData
  set qs := q.shrink with hqs
  haveI : ∀ i, (((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj M).over (g ⁻¹ᵁ (qs.X i))).IsQuasicoherent :=
    fun i => isQuasicoherent_over_preimage g M qs i
  exact SheafOfModules.IsQuasicoherent.of_coversTop ((Scheme.Modules.pullback g).obj M)
    (fun i => g ⁻¹ᵁ (qs.X i)) (coversTop_preimage g M qs)

/-- **(Piece A, target) Quasi-coherence is preserved under pullback along `fromSpec`.**
For `M` quasi-coherent on `X` and an affine open `U`, the pullback of `M` along the affine immersion
`hU.fromSpec : Spec Γ(X, U) ⟶ X` is quasi-coherent. The `g := hU.fromSpec` instance of
`isQuasicoherent_pullback_of_isOpenImmersion` (`fromSpec` is an open immersion). This is the
QC-pullback input the gap2 close feeds to gap1. Project-local. -/
theorem isQuasicoherent_pullback_fromSpec (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent]
    {U : X.Opens} (hU : IsAffineOpen U) :
    ((Scheme.Modules.pullback hU.fromSpec).obj M).IsQuasicoherent :=
  isQuasicoherent_pullback_of_isOpenImmersion hU.fromSpec M

/-- **gap2 keystone (`lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen`): basic-open section localization for
a quasi-coherent sheaf on an arbitrary scheme.** For `M` quasi-coherent on `X`, an affine open `U`,
and `f : Γ(X, U)`, the section restriction `Γ(M, U) → Γ(M, X.basicOpen f)` is
`IsLocalizedModule (powers f)` over `Γ(X, U)`. Assembles the QC-pullback (Piece A,
`isQuasicoherent_pullback_fromSpec`) → gap1 (`isIso_fromTildeΓ_of_isQuasicoherent`) → the eqToHom
bridge (Piece B, `isLocalizedModule_basicOpen_of_hP1`). Project-local: closes gap2. -/
theorem isLocalizedModule_basicOpen (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent]

support/properness predicates of `blueprint/src/chapters/Picard_QuotScheme.tex`,

annihilator ideal sheaf for sheaves of modules on a scheme, nor a schematic-support
or proper-support predicate, so they are built here.

The annihilator is packaged via `Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdeals`, exactly mirroring
Mathlib's `Scheme.Hom.ker` (which is `ofIdeals fun U ↦ RingHom.ker (f.app U).hom`):
`ofIdeals` produces *the largest ideal sheaf contained in* an arbitrary affine-local
family of ideals, so the structure's `map_ideal_basicOpen` coherence is discharged
internally and need not be supplied at definition time. The basic-open coherence that
makes the local annihilators agree with `ofIdeals` (the analogue of `Hom.ker_apply`,
`def:modules_annihilator`) is the separate characterization lemma `annihilator_ideal`,
which depends on the not-yet-closed QCoh→localization bridge
`isLocalizedModule_basicOpen` (`lem:qcoh_section_localization_basicOpen`) together with
the algebra engine `Module.annihilator_isLocalizedModule_eq_map`
(`lem:annihilator_localization_eq_map`); see the handoff in
`task_results/.../QuotScheme.md`. -/

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

(`def:modules_annihilator`).

`Ann_{Γ(X,U)}(Γ(F,U))` of the `Γ(X,U)`-module of sections `Γ(F,U)`. The ideal sheaf
is assembled with `Scheme.IdealSheafData.ofIdeals`, the largest ideal sheaf contained
in that affine-local family — exactly the construction used for `Scheme.Hom.ker`. This
sidesteps proving the basic-open coherence (`map_ideal_basicOpen`) at definition time;
the identity `(annihilator F).ideal U = Ann_{Γ(X,U)}(Γ(F,U))` is the downstream
characterization lemma (`annihilator_ideal`, blocked on the QCoh localization bridge).

This is a project-local primitive: Mathlib does not carry an annihilator ideal sheaf
for sheaves of modules on a scheme. -/
noncomputable def annihilator (F : X.Modules) : X.IdealSheafData :=
  IdealSheafData.ofIdeals fun U => Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)

of the characterization; the reverse inclusion is the basic-open coherence blocked on
`isLocalizedModule_basicOpen`. Project-local because `annihilator` is. -/

  IdealSheafData.ideal_ofIdeals_le _ _

4051	\subsection{Iter-187 analogist-licensed named substrate gaps}
4052	\label{sec:quot_analogist_gaps}
4053	
4054	The iter-187 \texttt{mathlib-analogist quotscheme-isbasechange-tilde}
4055	verdict (see \texttt{analogies/quotscheme-isbasechange-tilde.md})
4056	identified two distinct Mathlib substrate gaps at the pinned commit
4057	\texttt{b80f227}. Both pins are now closed axiom-clean:
4058	\cref{lem:tildeIso_of_isQuasicoherent_isAffineOpen} via the gap1/gap2
4059	union-merge substrate, and \cref{lem:pullback_tildeIso} (2026-07-03,
4060	T12) by the adjoint-uniqueness route through
4061	\cref{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib} and
4062	\cref{lem:pullbackTilde_gammaBridge} below.
4063	
4064	\begin{lemma}[Tilde--global-sections adjunction on an affine scheme]
4065	  \label{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib}
4066	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.tilde.adjunction}
4067	  \mathlibok
4068	  \textit{Provided by Mathlib (\texttt{Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Modules.Tilde}).}
4069	  For a commutative ring \(R\), the tilde functor
4070	  \(\widetilde{(\cdot)} : \mathrm{Mod}_{R} \to (\Spec R).\mathrm{Modules}\)
4071	  is left adjoint to the global-sections functor
4072	  \(\Gamma(\Spec R, -) : (\Spec R).\mathrm{Modules} \to \mathrm{Mod}_{R}\)
4073	  (\texttt{moduleSpecΓFunctor}); the unit is the isomorphism
4074	  \(M \to \Gamma(\widetilde M, \top)\) and the counit is the
4075	  tilde--\(\Gamma\) comparison
4076	  \(\widetilde{\Gamma(\mathcal N, \top)} \to \mathcal N\)
4077	  (\texttt{fromTildeΓ}). Mathlib also supplies the two companion
4078	  adjunctions used with it below: extension--restriction of scalars
4079	  \(B \otimes_A - \dashv \mathrm{res}_\varphi\)
4080	  (\texttt{ModuleCat.extendRestrictScalarsAdj}) and
4081	  pullback--pushforward \(\pi^* \dashv \pi_*\) for sheaves of modules
4082	  over schemes (\texttt{Scheme.Modules.pullbackPushforwardAdjunction}).
4083	\end{lemma}
4084	
4085	\begin{lemma}[Global sections of the pushforward as restricted scalars]
4086	  \label{lem:pullbackTilde_gammaBridge}
4087	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.pullbackTilde_gammaBridge}
4088	  \leanok
4089	  \uses{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib, lem:modules_pullback_mathlib}
4090	  For a ring homomorphism \(\varphi : A \to B\) with
4091	  \(\pi = \Spec\varphi : \Spec B \to \Spec A\), the two functors
4092	  \((\Spec B).\mathrm{Modules} \to \mathrm{Mod}_{A}\)
4093	  \[
4094	    \mathcal N \longmapsto \Gamma(\Spec A,\, \pi_{*}\mathcal N)
4095	    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
4096	    \mathcal N \longmapsto \mathrm{res}_{\varphi}\, \Gamma(\Spec B,\, \mathcal N)
4097	  \]
4098	  (global sections of the pushforward, with \(A\) acting through
4099	  \(\Gamma(\pi^{\sharp})\); respectively global sections, with \(A\)
4100	  acting through \(\varphi\)) are naturally isomorphic.
4101	\end{lemma}
4102	\begin{proof}
4103	  \leanok
4104	  \uses{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib, lem:modules_pullback_mathlib}
4105	  On carriers the component at \(\mathcal N\) is restriction of sections
4106	  along the equality of opens \(\pi^{-1}(\Spec A) = \Spec B\), a
4107	  bijection. It is \(A\)-linear: for \(a \in A\) the action on the
4108	  source is by \(\Gamma(\pi^{\sharp})(\iota_A(a))\) and on the target by
4109	  \(\iota_B(\varphi(a))\), where
4110	  \(\iota_R : R \cong \Gamma(\Spec R, \mathcal O)\) is the canonical
4111	  identification; these agree by naturality of \(\iota\) in \(R\)
4112	  applied to \(\varphi\) (that is,
4113	  \(\Gamma(\pi^{\sharp}) \circ \iota_A = \iota_B \circ \varphi\)),
4114	  combined with semilinearity of section restriction for the module
4115	  sheaf \(\mathcal N\). Naturality in \(\mathcal N\) is naturality of
4116	  section restriction against module-sheaf morphisms.
4117	\end{proof}
4118	
4119	\begin{lemma}[Pullback of tilde is tilde of base change (Stacks 01HQ)]
4120	  \label{lem:pullback_tildeIso}
4121	  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.pullback_tildeIso}
4122	  \leanok
4123	  \uses{def:quot_pullback_app_isoTensor}
4124	  \textit{Source: Stacks~\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01HQ}{01HQ}
4125	  / \href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BJ8}{0BJ8} (pullback of
4126	  quasi-coherent modules along a Spec morphism).}
4127	  For a ring homomorphism \(\varphi : A \to B\) and an \(A\)-module
4128	  \(M\), there is a canonical iso between the pullback of the
4129	  tilde-sheaf and the tilde of the base-changed module:
4130	  \[
4131	    (\mathtt{Scheme.Modules.pullback}\, (\mathrm{Spec.map}\, \varphi)).\mathrm{obj}\,
4132	      (\widetilde{M})
4133	    \;\cong\;
4134	    \widetilde{B \otimes_A M}.
4135	  \]
4136	  Mathlib \texttt{b80f227} ships
4137	  \texttt{PullbackFree.lean:122 pullbackObjFreeIso} for \emph{free} sheaves
4138	  only — the general-module form (Stacks 01HQ) is unowned.
4139	\end{lemma}
4140	\begin{proof}
4141	  \leanok
4142	  \uses{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib, lem:pullbackTilde_gammaBridge,
4143	    def:quot_pullback_app_isoTensor}
4144	  Write \(\pi = \Spec\varphi : \Spec B \to \Spec A\). Both composite
4145	  functors
4146	  \[
4147	    \mathrm{Mod}_{A} \xrightarrow{\ \widetilde{(\cdot)}\ }
4148	      (\Spec A).\mathrm{Modules} \xrightarrow{\ \pi^{*}\ }
4149	      (\Spec B).\mathrm{Modules}
4150	    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
4151	    \mathrm{Mod}_{A} \xrightarrow{\ B \otimes_A -\ } \mathrm{Mod}_{B}
4152	      \xrightarrow{\ \widetilde{(\cdot)}\ } (\Spec B).\mathrm{Modules}
4153	  \]
4154	  are left adjoints: the first of
4155	  \(\mathcal N \mapsto \Gamma(\Spec A, \pi_{*}\mathcal N)\) (compose the
4156	  tilde--\(\Gamma\) adjunction on \(\Spec A\),
4157	  \cref{lem:tilde_gamma_adjunction_mathlib}, with
4158	  \(\pi^{*} \dashv \pi_{*}\)), the second of
4159	  \(\mathcal N \mapsto \mathrm{res}_{\varphi}\,\Gamma(\Spec B, \mathcal N)\)
4160	  (compose extension--restriction of scalars along \(\varphi\) with the
4161	  tilde--\(\Gamma\) adjunction on \(\Spec B\)). By
4162	  \cref{lem:pullbackTilde_gammaBridge} the two right adjoints are
4163	  naturally isomorphic, so uniqueness of left adjoints yields a natural
4164	  isomorphism of the two composites; its component at \(M\) is the
4165	  required isomorphism
4166	  \(\pi^{*}\widetilde M \cong \widetilde{B \otimes_A M}\).
4167	
4168	  For the section-level identity, apply the unit compatibility of the
4169	  left-adjoint-uniqueness isomorphism at \(m \in M\): the unit of the
4170	  first composed adjunction sends \(m\) to the canonical base map
4171	  (\cref{def:quot_pullback_app_isoTensor}, at \(V = U = \top\)) of the
4172	  global section of \(\widetilde M\) attached to \(m\), while the unit
4173	  of the second sends \(m\) to the global section of
4174	  \(\widetilde{B \otimes_A M}\) attached to \(1 \otimes m\); the
4175	  compatibility square states precisely that the isomorphism carries
4176	  the former to the latter.
4177	\end{proof}
4178

4180	\label{sec:quot_qcqs_section_localization}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lemma-widetilde-pullback}
Let
$(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = (\Spec(S), \mathcal{O}_{\Spec(S)})$,
$(Y, \mathcal{O}_Y) = (\Spec(R), \mathcal{O}_{\Spec(R)})$
be affine schemes.
Let $\psi : (X, \mathcal{O}_X) \to (Y, \mathcal{O}_Y)$ be a
morphism of affine schemes, corresponding to the ring map
$\psi^\sharp : R \to S$ (see Lemma \ref{lemma-category-affine-schemes}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item We have $\psi^* \widetilde M = \widetilde{S \otimes_R M}$
functorially in the $R$-module $M$.
\item We have $\psi_* \widetilde N = \widetilde{N_R}$ functorially
in the $S$-module $N$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
The first assertion follows from the identification in
Lemma \ref{lemma-compare-constructions}
and the result of Modules, Lemma \ref{modules-lemma-restrict-quasi-coherent}.
The second assertion follows from the fact
that $\psi^{-1}(D(f)) = D(\psi^\sharp(f))$ and hence
$$
\psi_* \widetilde N(D(f)) = \widetilde N(D(\psi^\sharp(f))) =
N_{\psi^\sharp(f)} = (N_R)_f = \widetilde{N_R}(D(f))
$$
as desired.
\end{proof}

\noindent
Lemma \ref{lemma-widetilde-pullback} above says in particular

morphism of affine schemes, corresponding to the ring map
$\psi^\sharp : R \to S$ (see Lemma \ref{lemma-category-affine-schemes}).
\begin{enumerate}
\item We have $\psi^* \widetilde M = \widetilde{S \otimes_R M}$
functorially in the $R$-module $M$.
\item We have $\psi_* \widetilde N = \widetilde{N_R}$ functorially
in the $S$-module $N$.
\end{enumerate}

The first assertion follows from the identification in

The second assertion follows from the fact

\label{lemma-quasi-coherent-affine}
Let $(X, \mathcal{O}_X) = (\Spec(R), \mathcal{O}_{\Spec(R)})$
be an affine scheme. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a
quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Then
$\mathcal{F}$ is isomorphic to the sheaf associated to
the $R$-module $\Gamma(X, \mathcal{F})$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Since every standard open $D(f)$ is quasi-compact we see that
$X$ is locally quasi-compact, i.e., every point has a fundamental

Definition \ref{topology-definition-locally-quasi-compact}.

there exists an open neighbourhood $x \in U \subset X$ such that

\begin{lemma}
\label{lemma-annihilator-flat-base-change}
Let $R \to S$ be a flat ring map. Let $M$ be an $R$-module and
$m \in M$. Then $\text{Ann}_R(m) S = \text{Ann}_S(m \otimes 1)$.
If $M$ is a finite $R$-module, then
$\text{Ann}_R(M) S = \text{Ann}_S(M \otimes_R S)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
Set $I = \text{Ann}_R(m)$. By definition there is an exact sequence
$0 \to I \to R \to M$ where the map $R \to M$ sends $f$ to $fm$. Using
flatness we obtain an exact sequence
$0 \to I \otimes_R S \to S \to M \otimes_R S$ which proves the first
assertion. If $m_1, \ldots, m_n$ is a set of generators of $M$
then $\text{Ann}_R(M) = \bigcap \text{Ann}_R(m_i)$. Similarly
$\text{Ann}_S(M \otimes_R S) = \bigcap \text{Ann}_S(m_i \otimes 1)$.
Set $I_i = \text{Ann}_R(m_i)$. Then it suffices to show that
$\bigcap_{i = 1, \ldots, n} (I_i S) = (\bigcap_{i = 1, \ldots, n} I_i)S$.
This is Lemma \ref{lemma-flat-intersect-ideals}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}
\label{lemma-support-closed}
Let $R$ be a ring and let $M$ be an $R$-module.
If $M$ is finite, then $\text{Supp}(M)$ is closed.
More precisely, if $I = \text{Ann}(M)$ is the annihilator of $M$, then
$V(I) = \text{Supp}(M)$.
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
We will show that $V(I) = \text{Supp}(M)$.

\medskip\noindent
Suppose $\mathfrak p \in \text{Supp}(M)$. Then $M_{\mathfrak p} \not = 0$.
Choose an element $m \in M$ whose image in $M_\mathfrak p$ is nonzero.
Then the annihilator of $m$ is contained in $\mathfrak p$ by construction
of the localization $M_\mathfrak p$. Hence
a fortiori $I = \text{Ann}(M)$ must be contained in $\mathfrak p$.

\medskip\noindent
Conversely, suppose that $\mathfrak p \not \in \text{Supp}(M)$.
Then $M_{\mathfrak p} = 0$.
Let $x_1, \ldots, x_r \in M$ be generators.
By Lemma \ref{lemma-localization-colimit} there exists
an $f \in R$, $f\not\in \mathfrak p$ such that
$x_i/1 = 0$ in $M_f$. Hence $f^{n_i} x_i = 0$ for some $n_i \geq 1$.
Hence $f^nM = 0$ for $n = \max\{n_i\}$ as desired.
\end{proof}
